To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the FGF8b isoform of fibroblast growth factor-8, which is expressed by normal and tumor prostates, is a growth and tumorigenesis factor for NIH3T3 fibroblastic cells and DU145 human prostatic carcinoma cells, and that its overexpression in antisense orientation is effective in reversing these effects.

the N-terminal portions of the human fibroblast growth factor-8 (hFGF8) isoform are capable of transforming NIH3T3 fibroblasts and that overexpression of the full-length or N-terminal portions of hFGF8 in antisense orientation in DU145 cells inhibits cell growth in vitro and in vivo.

FGF8 is expressed in human prostatic epithelial and carcinoma cells, and its overexpression in NIH3T 3 fibroblasts and in the prostatic carcinoma DU-145 cells induces their morphologic and growth transformation, and that the N-terminal region of the protein is responsible for the observed biologic effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of growth factors that are important in prostatic epithelium.
the identification of growth factors in prostatic carcinoma cells and the elucidation of their role in the pathogenesis of this disease.
identifying the biologic functions of FGF8 in normal and malignant human prostatic cells, and in developing novel strategies for the control of prostatic cancer growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the N-terminal region of FGF8, which includes the signal peptide domain, is the major functional domain of the molecule in terms of its ability to confer the morphologic transforming, soft agar clonogenecity and anchorage-independent properties in the murine fibroblast cell system.
FGF8 is not a growth factor for normal prostatic epithelial cell and that it may play a role in prostatic carcinogenesis.
FGF8 is a potent mitogenic and morphogenic factor for NIH3T3 fibroblasts and DU145 human prostatic carcinoma cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

FGF8 may play a role in the development of prostatic carcinoma, and that the N-terminal domain of the molecule may be the critical domain in mediating its biologic activities in the cell systems examined.

the N-terminal region of human FGF-8b is sufficient to induce the morphologic transformation of NIH3T3 and DU145 cells, and that antisense expression of FGF-8 can reverse the transformed phenotypes of NIH3T 3 cells and inhibit the growth and tumorigenecity of DU145 cells.
the FGF8 protein is a potential target for anti-prostate cancer drug design.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FGF8b is a growth factor that can be used as a target for cancer treatment, especially in prostate cancer.
FGF8 is an important factor for prostate cancer progression.

the N-terminal portion of the human FGF8b protein, which is the major isoform expressed in prostatic cells, has a growth-promoting activity in NIH3T cells, and that the expression of this portion in antisense orientation is capable of inhibiting the growth and tumorigenesis of human DU145 prostatic carcinoma cells.
